title.sl: Nekdo, nekaj, nikjer: some-, any-, no-, every-
title.de: Jemand, etwas, nirgends: some-, any-, no-, every-
title.it: Qualcuno, qualcosa, da nessuna parte: some-, any-, no-, every-
title.en: Someone, anything, nowhere: some-, any-, no-, every-

rule.sl:
Prvi del je kot pri **some** in **any**, zadnji pove kdo, kaj ali kje: **-one** ali **-body** za osebo, **-thing** za stvar, **-where** za kraj.

**some-** v trdilnih stavkih in ponudbah: **Someone is at the door.** (Nekdo je pri vratih.) **Would you like something to drink?**

**any-** v zanikanih stavkih in večini vprašanj: **I can't see anyone.** (Nikogar ne vidim.) **Did you buy anything?** (Si kaj kupil{m:|f:a}?)

**no-** ima ne že v sebi, zato je glagol trdilen: **I saw nothing.** je isto kot **I didn't see anything.** (Nič nisem videl{m:|f:a}.) Samo ena nikalnica, nikoli *I didn't see nothing.* **No one** lahko začne stavek: **No one came.** (Nihče ni prišel.)

**every-** za vse, z glagolom v ednini: **Everyone is at the inn.** (Vsi so v gostilni.), nikoli *Everyone are.*

Za njimi pride pridevnik ali **to** + glagol: **something nice** (nekaj lepega), **something to eat**. **else** pomeni drug: **anything else?**, **someone else**.
rule.de:
Der erste Teil ist wie bei **some** und **any**, der letzte sagt wer, was oder wo: **-one** oder **-body** für eine Person, **-thing** für eine Sache, **-where** für einen Ort.

**some-** im bejahten Satz und im Angebot: **Someone is at the door.** (Jemand ist an der Tür.) **Would you like something to drink?**

**any-** im verneinten Satz und in den meisten Fragen: **I can't see anyone.** (Ich sehe niemanden.) **Did you buy anything?** (Hast du etwas gekauft?)

**no-** hat das Nein schon in sich, das Verb bleibt bejaht: **I saw nothing.** ist dasselbe wie **I didn't see anything.** (Ich habe nichts gesehen.) Nur eine Verneinung, nie *I didn't see nothing.* **No one** kann den Satz beginnen: **No one came.** (Niemand ist gekommen.)

**every-** für alle, mit dem Verb im Singular: **Everyone is at the inn.** (Alle sind im Gasthaus.), nie *Everyone are.*

Danach kommt ein Adjektiv oder **to** + Verb: **something nice** (etwas Schönes), **something to eat**. **else** heißt sonst: **anything else?**, **someone else**.
rule.it:
La prima parte è come **some** e **any**, l'ultima dice chi, che cosa o dove: **-one** o **-body** per una persona, **-thing** per una cosa, **-where** per un luogo.

**some-** nelle frasi affermative e nelle offerte: **Someone is at the door.** (C'è qualcuno alla porta.) **Would you like something to drink?**

**any-** nelle frasi negative e in quasi tutte le domande: **I can't see anyone.** (Non vedo nessuno.) **Did you buy anything?** (Hai comprato qualcosa?)

**no-** ha già il no dentro, quindi il verbo resta affermativo: **I saw nothing.** è come **I didn't see anything.** (Non ho visto niente.) Una sola negazione, mai *I didn't see nothing.* **No one** può aprire la frase: **No one came.** (Non è venuto nessuno.)

**every-** per tutti, con il verbo al singolare: **Everyone is at the inn.** (Sono tutti alla locanda.), mai *Everyone are.*

Dopo viene un aggettivo o **to** + verbo: **something nice** (qualcosa di bello), **something to eat**. **else** vuol dire altro: **anything else?**, **someone else**.
rule.en:
The first part is as with **some** and **any**, the last says who, what or where: **-one** or **-body** for a person, **-thing** for a thing, **-where** for a place.

**some-** in yes sentences and offers: **Someone is at the door.** **Would you like something to drink?**

**any-** in no sentences and most questions: **I can't see anyone.** **Did you buy anything?**

**no-** has the no in it, so the verb stays yes: **I saw nothing.** is the same as **I didn't see anything.** One negative only: **I didn't see anything.** (never *I didn't see nothing.*) **No one** can open a sentence: **No one came.**

**every-** for all, with a singular verb: **Everyone is at the inn.** (never *Everyone are at the inn.*)

After them comes an adjective or **to** + a verb: **something nice**, **something to eat**. **else** means other: **anything else?**, **someone else**.

examples.en: Meg is somewhere on the fell.
examples.it: Meg è da qualche parte sul monte.

examples.en: Did you buy anything at the market?
examples.de: Hast du auf dem Markt etwas gekauft?

examples.en: Everyone is at the inn tonight.
examples.de: Heute Abend sind alle im Gasthaus.

examples.en: Would you like something to eat?

rule.sl: **someone, something, somewhere**: trdilno, ponudba. **anyone, anything, anywhere**: zanikano, vprašanje. **no one, nothing, nowhere**: glagol trdilen. **everyone, everything, everywhere**: glagol v ednini.
rule.de: **someone, something, somewhere**: bejaht, Angebot. **anyone, anything, anywhere**: verneint, Frage. **no one, nothing, nowhere**: das Verb bejaht. **everyone, everything, everywhere**: das Verb im Singular.
rule.it: **someone, something, somewhere**: affermativa, offerta. **anyone, anything, anywhere**: negativa, domanda. **no one, nothing, nowhere**: verbo affermativo. **everyone, everything, everywhere**: verbo al singolare.
rule.en: **someone, something, somewhere**: yes, offers. **anyone, anything, anywhere**: no, questions. **no one, nothing, nowhere**: the verb stays yes. **everyone, everything, everywhere**: a singular verb.

examples.en: Everyone is at the inn tonight.
examples.de: Heute Abend sind alle im Gasthaus.

tip.sl: 💡 Samo ena nikalnica: **I saw nothing.** ali **I didn't see anything.**, nikoli *I didn't see nothing.*
tip.it: 💡 Una sola negazione: **I saw nothing.** o **I didn't see anything.**, mai *I didn't see nothing.*
tip.en: 💡 One negative only: **I didn't see anything.** (never *I didn't see nothing.*)
